title: Page residency heatmap and opportunistic rehome protocol for paged-KV
creator: Lina Zhang
description:
Problem statement: As tenant working sets grow and sequence length distributions vary, our paged KV allocator exhibits fragmentation that increases decode time due to extra scattering and forces cold evictions that trigger expensive prefill/restore cycles. Existing eviction heuristics (LRU-ish with coarse occupancy thresholds) frequently evict small high-reuse fragments or leave many small free fragments that block future coalescing. We need a low-risk protocol to reduce fragmentation, surface actionable residency telemetry, and opportunistically move fragments to improve compactability without violating tail-latency SLOs.

Goal: Build a page residency heatmap + opportunistic rehome protocol to: 1) surface per-shard and cross-shard residency heatmaps used by kernel selection and prefill scheduling; 2) proactively regroup hot fragments into contiguous pages to reduce decode scatter and increase contiguous-run kernel utilization; 3) perform rehomes (cooperative relocate of fragments) during low-util intervals to defragment without impacting foreground decode; 4) feed compactability score to eviction policy so we prefer evicting fragments that free contiguous space.

Design summary:
- Telemetry & Heatmap: each KV fragment emits a lightweight touch counter and last-touch epoch. Shard-local aggregator buckets fragments into a fixed grid heatmap (hot/warm/cold) with decay. Heatmaps are rolled up to a global planner at configurable cadence (default 30s). Heatmap keys are tenant, model variant, and page-anchor.
- Compactability score: compute per-page compactability = fraction of capacity that can be freed by relocating N smallest fragments (N tunable). Pages with high compactability are prioritized for opportunistic reclamation.
- Opportunistic rehome protocol: when a page's compactability > threshold and system idle score > idle_threshold, a background coordinator claims a target page and migrates selected fragments into a destination page pool. Migration is copy-on-write: new fragments are written into destination page, pointer swap is atomic, old fragments marked for reclamation. The protocol uses rate limits per-shard and global token bucket to avoid competing with decode paths.
- Kernel hints & scheduling: kernel selector consults heatmap + compactability to prefer contiguous-run kernels for pages with low fragmentation; for highly fragmented pages it selects scatter-aware kernels or issues partial-prefill to consolidate KV before decode. Prefill scheduler uses heatmap to prioritize prefetch budget to fragments in the warm band that are rising in touch frequency.
- Safety & fallbacks: migrations carry sequence-numbered manifests; any failure reverts to original pointers. Migrations only proceed if estimated copy time < tail-safe-window computed from recent p95 decode latency. Coordinator backs off and retries exponentially.

Metrics and success criteria:
- Reduce average decode scatter reads per request by >= 25% on representative benchmark suite.
- Reduce eviction-induced prefill restore latency (95th) by >= 20% for multi-tenant traces.
- Decrease fragmentation score (internal metric) by >= 30% over 24h on stressed clusters.
- No regression to p99 decode latency > 1.05x baseline during canary.

Implementation plan:
1) Prototype heatmap aggregator in simulator (offline) + add lightweight touch telemetry to dev shard image. (2 wks)
2) Implement compactability calculator and background rehome coordinator with rate limiting; expose debug flags. (3 wks)
3) Integrate kernel-selector hooks to consume heatmap and compactability; add prefill scoring changes. (2 wks)
4) Run cluster simulator and offline workload replay to tune thresholds (1 wk)
5) Shadow run (no-op migrations; compute scores and compare) on prod-like cluster for 2 weeks.
6) Canary: enable migrations 1% of traffic -> 10% -> 50% with monitoring runbooks.

Rollout notes: start with read-only heatmap exports (no migration) to collect baseline metrics. Canary migrations only on non-critical tenant lanes and during low traffic windows.

Risks and mitigations:
- Migration thrash under sustained high load: mitigate by aggressive idle-score gating + global token-bucket and per-shard debt accounting.
- Pointer-swap races with concurrent decode: use epoched manifests and atomic CAS in page table; add assert-mode in dev to detect races.
- Increased memory amplification during migration: bound temporary staging pool and fail migrations when staging > X% of page pool.
- Telemetry overhead: heatmap buckets aggregate in-shard and are decayed; we cap emission frequency to 1/s per hot fragment and 0.1/s otherwise.

Alternatives considered:
- Heavyweight stop-the-world defrag on a shard (rejected: tail-latency impact).
- Global compaction service that pauses decodes per shard (rejected: complexity and customer impact).
- Increasing page size to reduce fragmentation (rejected: changes kernel assumptions and increases padding waste).
acceptance_criteria: Heatmap exporter running in shadow mode on prod-like cluster for 2 weeks with no errors
Simulator shows >=25% reduction in scatter reads on benchmark suite
Canary migrations run at 1% with no p99 regression >1.05x baseline
Eviction policy consumes compactability score and prefers contiguous freeing of pages
End-to-end RoI dashboard: fragment_count, fragmentation_score, migrate_ops, migration_failures, p95_prestore_latency
comments: 2026-02-15 — Lina Zhang: Spiked heatmap proto in simulator. Initial traces show clear recurring hot spans per tenant; posting proto graphs to the confluence doc.

2026-02-19 — Owen McCarthy: Implemented per-fragment touch counters in dev shard. Telemetry overhead measured at ~0.6% CPU at 1Hz emission; acceptable. Opened PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/12345

2026-02-26 — PM review (Marco Ruiz): Strong +1 on heatmap visibility. Requested that compactability score is exposed to the console and the rollout include a customer-impact flag to opt-out high-risk tenants.
2026-03-01 — Team chat: Decided to use staging pool size 8 pages and token-bucket of 50KB/s global for migrations as initial conservative limits.
2026-03-04 — Owen McCarthy: Added atomic manifest swap and fallback path. Running cluster replay to verify no pointer races.
